control_flow: followInTheDark: if the right light is below 60 %, go deep-dark branch; else call avoidWalls.
Deep-dark branch: if the left light is below 45 %, curve left; else if the line tracker reads above 95 % (white band), curve right; else call avoidWalls.
avoidWalls: if the left light is below 70 %, check side obstacles (left seen: turn right 20°; right seen: turn left 20°; else driveInTheDark); else driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if the left light is below 70 %, drive forward 30 %; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Follow the line in bright light, and keep following it through a dark tunnel, steering with the light sensors where the line is hard to see.

decision_points.condition: in dim light: obstacle on the LEFT, else obstacle on the RIGHT

left light below 70 %: drives forward at 30 %
left light 70 % or more: calls stopAtWall

scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line in bright light, with nothing ahead and no tunnel around it.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker goes between black and the floor as the robot steers.
scenarios.title: Follows the line in bright light

You didn't say where the line ends or what it should do there.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line along its course in the bright light.

scenarios.coded_response: In dim light it drives straight and turns away from a side wall that comes into view; deeper, where the right light is below 60 %, it curves right when the line tracker sees the white band and curves left when the left light is below 45 %.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot follows a line in bright light into a dark tunnel; as it goes in, the light on it falls and the tunnel may bend.
scenarios.trigger: The light around the robot falls below the program's thresholds, and the line tracker sees black and white.
scenarios.title: Follows the line in the dark (through a tunnel)
assumptions: You didn't say what it should do at a wall straight ahead inside the tunnel, or how far it should get.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It keeps following the line through the dark tunnel and comes out without bumping into the walls.

scenarios.initial_condition: The robot follows a line in bright light toward a wall that the line runs into.
scenarios.trigger: The front obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall ahead
assumptions: You didn't mention walls, but a robot following a line should not drive into one, and the program has a stop for it.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops before the wall without bumping into it.

uncertainties: In a tunnel the light falls with depth, so the program's light thresholds switch at different depths (left below 70 % at about 7.5 cm, right below 60 % at about 10 cm, left below 45 % at about 13.75 cm in), and it changes behaviour several times as it drives in.
Deepest in the dark the left light is below 45 % and the program curves left before it ever reads the line, so there it may not actually follow the line.
In bright light on a plain floor the robot circles (it turned right 258° in 3 s): it needs a line under it to drive straight.
The loop has no waits, so the robot re-reads its sensors and changes its movement many times a second and wiggles.
In a tunnel both light sensors read by depth, so left and right read alike and the left/right comparisons mostly track how deep it is, not a real side.
